# Route Helpers — Comprehensive Study Guide

> **Module:** Phase 1 — Module 3 (Routing)
> **Topic:** Route Helpers
> **Target Audience:** Rails developers preparing for Senior/Lead roles

---

## 1. Overview

### What it is

**Route helpers** are Ruby methods that Rails auto-generates from your route definitions. They build URL paths and full URLs without hardcoding strings.

```ruby
# Route definition
resources :products

# Auto-generated helpers
products_path       # => "/products"
product_path(42)    # => "/products/42"
new_product_path    # => "/products/new"
edit_product_path(42) # => "/products/42/edit"

# _url variants include host
products_url        # => "http://localhost:3000/products"
product_url(42)     # => "http://localhost:3000/products/42"
```

Every named route gets **two helpers**: one ending in `_path`, one ending in `_url`.

### Why they exist

Route helpers are the glue between your route definitions and every place in your app that needs a URL. They ensure:

- **Consistency** — one source of truth in `routes.rb`
- **Refactoring safety** — change a route, all links update automatically
- **Parameter enforcement** — missing required params raise clear errors
- **Readability** — `product_path(@product)` is self-documenting

### When you use route helpers

| Location | Example | Helper type |
|---|---|---|
| Views | `link_to "Show", product_path(@product)` | `_path` |
| Controllers | `redirect_to products_path` | `_path` |
| Mailers | `order_url(@order)` | `_url` (needs host) |
| Background jobs | `product_url(@product, host: ENV['HOST'])` | `_url` |
| Tests | `get product_path(@product)` | `_path` |
| Serializers | `self: product_url(product)` | `_url` |

### Common misconceptions

| Misconception | Reality |
|---|---|
| "Helpers are defined manually" | Rails generates them automatically from named routes |
| "Only views have access to helpers" | Any class can `include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers` |
| "Helper names are random" | They follow strict conventions based on route definition |
| "`_path` and `_url` call different routes" | Same route — `_url` just adds host/protocol/port |

---

## 2. Core Concepts

### Naming Convention

Route helper names come from the route's **prefix** (the "Prefix" column in `bin/rails routes`):

```bash
$ bin/rails routes -g product

Prefix          Verb   URI Pattern              Controller#Action
products        GET    /products                products#index
new_product     GET    /products/new            products#new
product         GET    /products/:id            products#show
edit_product    GET    /products/:id/edit         products#edit
```

| Prefix | Path Helper | URL Helper |
|---|---|---|
| `products` | `products_path` | `products_url` |
| `new_product` | `new_product_path` | `new_product_url` |
| `product` | `product_path(id)` | `product_url(id)` |
| `edit_product` | `edit_product_path(id)` | `edit_product_url(id)` |

### `_path` vs `_url`

```ruby
# _path — relative path (no host)
product_path(42)
# => "/products/42"

# _url — absolute URL (includes host, protocol, port)
product_url(42)
# => "http://localhost:3000/products/42"
```

**When to use which:**

| Use `_path` | Use `_url` |
|---|---|
| Links within your app | Links in emails |
| Controller redirects | External notifications (SMS, push) |
| Same-domain API responses | RSS feeds, sitemaps |
| Tests (usually) | Background jobs |
| Turbo/Hotwire navigation | Open Graph / social sharing meta tags |

### Passing Parameters

```ruby
# Required segment params
product_path(42)                          # => "/products/42"
product_path(@product)                    # => calls @product.to_param

# Query string params (any extra hash key)
products_path(sort: 'asc', page: 2)         # => "/products?sort=asc&page=2"

# Format
product_path(42, format: :json)            # => "/products/42.json"

# Anchor
product_path(42, anchor: 'reviews')        # => "/products/42#reviews"

# Combined
products_path(sort: 'price', format: :json, page: 1)
# => "/products.json?sort=price&page=1"
```

### Nested Route Helpers

```ruby
resources :products do
  resources :reviews
end

# Helpers include parent name
product_reviews_path(@product)              # => "/products/42/reviews"
product_review_path(@product, @review)      # => "/products/42/reviews/7"
new_product_review_path(@product)           # => "/products/42/reviews/new"
edit_product_review_path(@product, @review) # => "/products/42/reviews/7/edit"
```

Parent always comes first in the argument list.

### Namespaced Route Helpers

```ruby
namespace :admin do
  resources :products
end

admin_products_path                         # => "/admin/products"
admin_product_path(42)                      # => "/admin/products/42"
new_admin_product_path                      # => "/admin/products/new"
```

Each namespace level adds a prefix segment to the helper name.

### Shallow Route Helpers

With `shallow: true`, you get **two sets** of helpers:

```ruby
resources :products do
  resources :reviews, shallow: true
end

# Nested (collection actions)
product_reviews_path(@product)              # => "/products/42/reviews"
new_product_review_path(@product)           # => "/products/42/reviews/new"

# Shallow (member actions)
review_path(@review)                        # => "/reviews/7"
edit_review_path(@review)                   # => "/reviews/7/edit"
```

## 3. Advanced Helpers

### `url_for` — Universal Helper

Works everywhere and accepts many input formats:

```ruby
url_for(@product)                           # polymorphic — show path
url_for([@product, @review])                # nested polymorphic
url_for(controller: 'products', action: 'show', id: 42)
url_for(action: 'index', only_path: true)   # current controller context
url_for(action: 'index', only_path: false)  # full URL
```

### Polymorphic Helpers

When the record type varies at runtime:

```ruby
polymorphic_path(@record)                   # show path for any AR model
polymorphic_url(@record)                    # show URL for any AR model
edit_polymorphic_path(@record)              # edit path
polymorphic_path([@parent, @child])         # nested

# Examples:
polymorphic_path(Product.find(1))           # => "/products/1"
polymorphic_path(Article.find(5))           # => "/articles/5"
polymorphic_path([@product, @review])       # => "/products/1/reviews/3"
```

### `link_to` and `button_to` Integration

Route helpers integrate directly with view helpers:

```ruby
link_to "Show Product", product_path(@product)
link_to "Show Product", @product                    # same — url_for internally
link_to "Delete", product_path(@product), method: :delete

button_to "Create", products_path, method: :post
```

Rails 7+ with Turbo:

```ruby
link_to "Delete", product_path(@product),
  data: { turbo_method: :delete, turbo_confirm: "Sure?" }
```

### `form_with` Integration

```ruby
# Automatically picks correct path and method
form_with model: @product do |f|
  # NEW product  → POST /products
  # EXISTING     → PATCH /products/:id
end

# Nested form
form_with model: [@product, @review] do |f|
  # NEW  → POST /products/:product_id/reviews
  # EXIST   → PATCH /products/:product_id/reviews/:id
end
```

### Custom/Member/Collection Helpers

```ruby
resources :products do
  collection { get :search }
  member { post :publish }
end

search_products_path                        # => "/products/search"
publish_product_path(@product)              # => "/products/42/publish"
```

Pattern: `{action}_{resource(s)}_path`

---

## 4. Including Helpers Outside Views

Views and controllers include route helpers automatically. Other classes need explicit inclusion:

### Mailers

```ruby
class OrderMailer < ApplicationMailer
  # ApplicationMailer already includes url_helpers

  def confirmation(order)
    @order = order
    @url = order_url(@order)  # works if default_url_options set
    mail(to: order.email, subject: "Confirmed")
  end
end
```

### Background Jobs

```ruby
class NotificationJob < ApplicationJob
  include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

  def perform(product_id)
    product = Product.find(product_id)
    url = product_url(product, host: ENV.fetch('APP_HOST'))
    # send notification with url
  end
end
```

### Serializers / Presenters

```ruby
class ProductSerializer
  include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

  def initialize(product, host:)
    @product = product
    @host = host
  end

  def as_json
    {
      id: @product.id,
      name: @product.name,
      url: product_url(@product, host: @host)
    }
  end
end
```

### Plain Ruby Classes

```ruby
class SitemapGenerator
  include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

  def initialize(default_url_options)
    @default_url_options = default_url_options
  end

  def url_options
    @default_url_options
  end

  def generate
    Product.find_each do |product|
      puts product_url(product)
    end
  end
end
```

When including manually, you may need to define `url_options` or pass `host:` explicitly.

## 5. Real Production Examples

### Example 1: E-Commerce Email with Order Link

```ruby
class OrderMailer < ApplicationMailer
  def shipped(order)
    @order = order
    @tracking_url = order_url(@order, host: 'shop.example.com')
    mail(to: order.email, subject: "Your order has shipped!")
  end
end
```

### Example 2: API Serializer with HATEOAS Links

```ruby
class Api::V1::ProductSerializer
  include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

  def serialize(product)
    {
      id: product.id,
      name: product.name,
      links: {
        self: product_url(product, host: api_host),
        reviews: product_reviews_url(product, host: api_host)
      }
    }
  end
end
```

### Example 3: Admin Dashboard with Namespaced Helpers

```erb
<%# app/views/admin/products/index.html.erb %>
<% @products.each do |product| %>
  <%= link_to product.name, admin_product_path(product) %>
  <%= link_to "Publish", publish_admin_product_path(product),
      data: { turbo_method: :post } %>
<% end %>

<%= link_to "New Product", new_admin_product_path %>
```

## 6. Common Mistakes

### Beginner

**1. Hardcoding URLs instead of helpers**

```ruby
# BAD
link_to "Product", "/products/#{@product.id}"

# GOOD
link_to "Product", @product
```

**2. Wrong argument order in nested helpers**

```ruby
# BAD — child before parent
review_path(@review, @product)

# GOOD — parent first
product_review_path(@product, @review)
```

**3. Using `_url` in views when `_path` suffices**

```ruby
# Unnecessary — _path works fine for same-domain links
link_to "Products", products_url

# Preferred
link_to "Products", products_path
```

### Mid-Level

**4. Missing host in mailers/jobs**

```ruby
# FAILS in Sidekiq/mailer
product_url(@product)
# ArgumentError: Missing host to link to!

# FIX
product_url(@product, host: 'example.com')
# OR configure default_url_options
```

**5. Not overriding `to_param` for slug-based routes**

```ruby
class Product < ApplicationRecord
  def to_param
    slug  # product_path(@product) => "/products/running-shoe"
  end
end
```

**6. Using stale helper after route change**

After renaming a route, grep the codebase for old helper names:

```bash
grep -r "old_helper_name" app/ test/
```

### Senior/Lead

**7. Helper usage in model callbacks**

Models should not generate URLs. Use presenters or mailers.

**8. Not setting `default_url_options` per environment**

```ruby
# config/environments/production.rb
config.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: 'shop.example.com', protocol: 'https' }
config.action_controller.default_url_options = { host: 'shop.example.com' }
```

---

## 7. Performance Considerations

Route helper calls are extremely fast (string interpolation from a template). No concerns for normal usage.

Potential issues:
- Calling helpers that trigger DB queries via custom `to_param`
- Generating millions of URLs in a sitemap — batch and cache

---

## 8. Security Considerations

- Never pass user input directly to `redirect_to` without validation
- Use `_path` (relative) in redirects to prevent open redirect attacks
- Set explicit `host:` in mailers — don't rely on user-controlled Host header

```ruby
# SAFE redirect
redirect_to product_path(@product)

# DANGEROUS
redirect_to params[:return_url]
```

---

## 9. Debugging

### Find Helper Name for a Route

```bash
bin/rails routes -g product
# Look at "Prefix" column
```

### Test Helper in Console

```ruby
include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
product_path(42)

# Or in rails console
app.product_path(42)
```

### Common Errors

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `undefined method 'product_path'` | Route not defined or not named | Check `bin/rails routes` |
| `No route matches { ... }` | Wrong/missing params | Verify required segments |
| `Missing host` | `_url` without host config | Set `default_url_options` |
| `ArgumentError: Missing required key: :id` | Forgot to pass ID | Pass all required params |

---

## 10. Best Practices

1. **Always use helpers** — never hardcode URL strings
2. **`_path` in app, `_url` in emails/jobs**
3. **Pass objects, not IDs** — `product_path(@product)` not `product_path(@product.id)`
4. **Override `to_param`** for slug-based URLs
5. **Include `url_helpers`** explicitly in mailers, jobs, serializers
6. **Configure `default_url_options`** per environment
7. **Grep for old helpers** after route changes

---

## 11. Anti-Patterns

| Anti-Pattern | Better Approach |
|---|---|
| `"/products/#{id}"` | `product_path(id)` |
| `_url` in every view link | `_path` for same-domain |
| URL generation in models | Presenters/serializers |
| `redirect_to params[:url]` | Validated redirect path |
| Manual query string building | Pass hash to helper |

---

## 12. Interview Questions

### Basic

**Q: What is the difference between `products_path` and `products_url`?**

**A:** `products_path` returns a relative path (`"/products"`). `products_url` returns a full URL with protocol and host (`"http://localhost:3000/products"`). Same route, different output format.

### Intermediate

**Q: How do nested route helpers work?**

**A:** Parent comes first in arguments: `product_review_path(@product, @review)` generates `/products/:product_id/reviews/:id`. Helper name combines both resources: `{parent}_{child}_path`.

### Senior

**Q: How do you use route helpers in a Sidekiq job that sends emails with links?**

**A:**
1. `include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers` in the job or mailer
2. Configure `config.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: '...', protocol: 'https' }`
3. Or pass `host:` explicitly: `product_url(@product, host: ENV['APP_HOST'])`
4. Never rely on request context — jobs have none

---

## 13. Practical Examples

### Complete Helper Reference for a Resource

```ruby
resources :products do
  collection { get :search }
  member { post :publish }
end

# Standard CRUD
products_path                               # GET    /products
products_url                                # full URL
new_product_path                            # GET    /products/new
product_path(42)                            # GET    /products/42
edit_product_path(42)                       # GET    /products/42/edit

# Custom actions
search_products_path                        # GET    /products/search
publish_product_path(42)                    # POST   /products/42/publish

# With options
products_path(page: 2, sort: 'asc')         # /products?page=2&sort=asc
product_path(42, format: :json)            # /products/42.json
```

### Controller Redirects

```ruby
class ProductsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @product = Product.create(product_params)
    redirect_to @product, notice: "Created!"          # polymorphic
  end

  def update
    @product.update(product_params)
    redirect_to products_path, status: :see_other     # collection
  end

  def destroy
    @product.destroy
    redirect_to products_path
  end
end
```

### Mailer Setup

```ruby
# config/environments/development.rb
config.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: 'localhost', port: 3000 }

# config/environments/production.rb
config.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: 'shop.example.com', protocol: 'https' }

# app/mailers/order_mailer.rb
class OrderMailer < ApplicationMailer
  def confirmation(order)
    @order = order
    @url = order_url(@order)
    mail(to: order.email, subject: "Order ##{order.id} Confirmed")
  end
end
```

## 14. Related Topics

- **Route Generation** — the process helpers use internally
- **Route Recognition** — the inverse process
- **Resourceful Routing** — generates standard helper sets
- **Namespaces** — affect helper prefixes
- **Shallow Routing** — creates dual helper sets

---

## 15. Summary

1. Route helpers = **auto-generated methods** from named routes
2. **`_path`** = relative, **`_url`** = absolute (needs host)
3. **Nested helpers**: parent first — `product_review_path(@product, @review)`
4. **Namespaced helpers**: prefix matches namespace — `admin_products_path`
5. **Include `url_helpers`** in mailers, jobs, serializers
6. **Never hardcode URLs** — always use helpers
7. **`polymorphic_path`** for variable record types

---

## 16. Cheat Sheet

```ruby
# Basic
products_path                               # /products
product_path(@product)                      # /products/42
new_product_path                            # /products/new
edit_product_path(@product)                 # /products/42/edit

# Options
products_path(page: 2, sort: 'asc')         # query params
product_path(42, format: :json)            # format segment
product_path(42, anchor: 'top')            # anchor

# Nested
product_review_path(@product, @review)      # /products/1/reviews/3

# Namespaced
admin_products_path                         # /admin/products

# Polymorphic
polymorphic_path(@record)                   # works for any model

# Outside views
include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

# Console
app.product_path(42)
```

## 17. Practice Exercises

### Easy

List all route helpers for a `resources :articles` declaration using `bin/rails routes`. Call each helper in the console.

### Medium

Build a mailer that sends an email with a link to an order's show page. Make it work in development, test, and production.

### Hard

Create a `SitemapGenerator` class that includes route helpers and generates XML sitemap URLs for all products, articles, and categories. Handle host configuration correctly.
